blind_notes: Every key (188 single, 4 multi, 3 numeric, 3 order, 6 matrix) matched my blind answers; octal modes 750, 644, 700 recomputed. Only soft doubts: T1-061 (PAT), T2-060 (SELinux), both listed.

options_only.method: 188 single-answer items converted to the v1 shape in a scratch copy and run through tools/options_only.py. Because the main reviewer had already read every stem, the options-only picks were made by a separate fresh agent that saw only blind.json; a first, contaminated self-run was discarded.

findings.issue: Port forwarding 443 to an internal server is DNAT in netfilter terms, but many network courses call it static PAT / port address translation; PAT is offered as a distractor and the explanation does not address it.
findings.fix: Replace PAT with a non-overlapping distractor (e.g. NAT64) or reword the stem to 'Which iptables/nftables NAT type'.

findings.issue: SELinux can also stop root deleting a file with normal mode bits, and ls -Z / getenforce are offered. Immutable (lsattr) is the intended answer but the stem gives no error text to rule SELinux out.
findings.fix: Add 'with Operation not permitted, and SELinux is disabled' to the stem, or swap the SELinux distractors.

findings.issue: Explanation mentions SIGINT (Ctrl+C), which is not among the options (SIGHUP, SIGSTOP, SIGKILL, SIGTERM); SIGHUP and SIGSTOP are not explained.
findings.fix: Explain SIGHUP and SIGSTOP instead of SIGINT.

findings.issue: In the fresh options-only pass, genuine guesses (G) were right 100/145 (69%, chance 25%), so many distractor sets are weak even where no single cue was named; overall 76% is under the 82% ceiling.
findings.fix: When rewriting the S items, also strengthen distractors in the troubleshooting and services domains.
